text:
lina: getting a flood of customer 502/504 errors on hosted inference since ~09:10 PT. spike in gateway 5xx rate and multiple orgs reporting timeouts. sample req id: rq_0a1b2c3d. any quick ideas?

maya: on it. can you paste a raw failing curl and a sample gateway log line? also which model/route?

lina: curl we ran: 
```
curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer sk_live_xxx' -d '{"input":"hello"}' https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
response: HTTP/1.1 502 Bad Gateway
body: {"error":" upstream timeout while waiting for kv prefix cache"} 
route: /v1/generate -> model=gpt-4-small, route=hosted-prod-us

maya: thanks. i'm seeing corresponding traces: gateway returned 502 after 6s waiting for prefix-cache. sending to eng-oncall. pinging raj.

ops-bot: incident created: #inc-3375002468-cache-dep-5xx (auto)

raj: i've started looking at the prefix cache layer (memcached cluster for pfx). summary so far: metric spikes for memcached connections and auth errors from host pool 3a/3b. memcached node 3b is flapping DNS -> connection resets. sample memcached stats excerpt:
```
STAT cmd_get 234567
STAT get_hits 120300
STAT get_misses 11400
STAT bytes_read 98765432
STAT curr_connections 1024
STAT conn_yields 512
END
```
also kernel logs show "connection reset by peer" and memcached auth (SASL) failures on 10.12.3.18. service health shows GC thrash on pod memcached-3b.

maya: could auth rotation be in progress? we rotated KMS creds an hour ago for some customers but that shouldn't affect cluster-level SASL.

raj: checked key rotation logs — nothing for cluster SASL. root cause looks like memcached process OOM loop on 3b due to sudden prefetch storm (many long-running prefix lookups from a few tenants), causing it to crash and flapping nodes and connection resets -> gateway waits on KV RPC and times out -> 502/504.

lina: customers are seeing user-visible failures. can we force gateway to bypass prefix cache for hosted-prod-us while we stabilize memcached?

raj: yes. quick mitigation options:
- toggle prefix-cache for route to "bypass" in the routing-config (Console -> Routes -> hosted-prod-us -> cache: bypass). this will add load to origin but avoid memcached dependency.
- add temporary rate-limit on prefetch fanout (we can drop fanout to 1 for aggressive tenants).
- cordon memcached-3b and restart the memcached deployment with extra heap.

maya: i'll apply bypass for /v1/generate on hosted-prod-us now and set a gradual rollback window.

maya: ACTION: switched route cache policy to BYPASS at 09:28 PT. please monitor error rates and latency.

ops-bot: deploy event: routing-config change by maya @ 09:28 PT (id cfg_3375002468).

raj: memcached-3b pod restarted and now stable. investigating why it hit OOM: possible prefetch misconfiguration on a tenant causing large fanout + long KV queries. grabbing heap profile.

lina: error rate dropped ~85% after bypass. a few long-tail timeouts remain as requests hit origin. customers notified.

tomo: good quick mitigation. can we also patch gateway to hard-fail prefix RPC faster so we don't wait 6s? maybe reduce prefix RPC timeout from 6s->500ms while memcached is unstable.

raj: agreed. short-term config change: TTL for prefix RPC to 500ms in gateway-feature-flags for hosted-prod-us. i'll do that after we confirm memcached cluster status. will also add an emergency rule to switch tenants with heavy prefetch to conservative fanout=1.

maya: notes for support / reproducible steps for postmortem:
1) reproduce locally with memcached dev cluster: run a script that issues many concurrent prefix-get requests with varying keys to simulate fanout. example load command:
```
ab -n 10000 -c 200 -p payload.json https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
```
2) capture gateway logs with trace id and memcached client logs: `kubectl logs -l app=gateway --since=1h` and `kubectl logs memcached-3b`
3) check memcached stats: `echo stats | nc 10.12.3.18 11211` and look for curr_connections / evictions / bytes_read spikes.
4) verify if any tenant-level prefetch config changed recently: Console -> Optimize -> Caching -> Prefetch rules.

raj: postmortem action items (initial):
- tune default prefetch fanout to 4 (was 16) and add per-tenant throttle.
- add memcached liveness probe tweaks and headroom memory buffer to avoid OOM loops.
- add shorter prefix RPC client timeout with exponential backoff and fast-fail route to origin.
- add alerting for memcached curr_connections > 800 and SASL auth failures > 5/min.

maya: customer comms: sent update to impacted tenants (org-acme, org-beta, org-gamma) with mitigation and ETA for permanent fix.

lina: thanks team. error budget for hosted-prod-us routes looks in recovery. closing slack thread when postmortem doc is created.

ops-bot: incident #inc-3375002468 updated: mitigated at 09:35 PT.

raj: filing postmortem stub now. assigning owners. will link to #postmortems when done.

tomo: nice work. follow up: ensure runbook includes bypass steps and the exact console paths.

lina: ack. will add runbook checklist items (bypass -> reduce prefix timeout -> cordon memcached node).

maya: last check: CPU and mem stable on memcached cluster. keeping bypass for 30m, then we evaluate turning prefix cache back on.

raj: final: re-enabled prefix-cache at 10:02 PT but with reduced prefetch fanout and new fail-fast timeout. monitoring for regressions.

lina: thread resolved.
